titles: CHAPTER THREE. On the immortality of the soul from the confession of the best philosophers and from reasons
I. Not the best: Epicurus, Lucretius, Dicaearchus, Panaetius, and the Stoics deny or dilute immortality
Stoics on the soul's duration; Cleanthes and Chrysippus; Pliny impiously mocks immortality
Peripatetic interpreters Alexander and Averroes; Pomponazzi; Galen vs Plato; Isidore of Pelusium
II. Paradox: some who acknowledge Scripture deny immortality — Sadducees; Arabians; John XXIII
Photinians imply mortality; Tertullian assigns body yet vindicates immortality
III. Best philosophers asserting immortality: Pherecydes, Pythagoras, metempsychosis; Druids, Brahmans, Pharisees
III continued. Among the Greeks Plato and Aristotle held soul-immortality certain and clear
IV. Among the Latins Cicero and Seneca vote for soul-immortality; Tertullian on what nature knows
V. Heap of reasons after authorities; Ficino and Petrus Gregorius; RATIO I from operations of intellect
REASON II from operations of will; REASON III from the soul's ultimate rest
REASON IV from inconveniences of the contrary; Wisdom 2; VI use of these reasons — Cap. 3 close
